# vendor/art/forge_line — the `mill` rail's concept sheets

Three chroma-keyed asset sheets for the mode-4 machine hall, **generated by
the project owner with ChatGPT and supplied to the build session on
2026-08-29**. First-party: authored for this rail, not taken from a pack.
That is the origin **as stated to me** — correct this paragraph if it is
wrong, because everything below is derived from it and `docs/92` cites it.

They are the *unmodified* files as supplied; `SHA256SUMS` records them.
`tools/gen_mill_assets.py` reads them at asset-generation time through
`tools/kit_import.py` and emits the rail's CHR, palettes and maps.

| file | native | holds |
|---|---|---|
| `frames_sheet.png` | 1448×1086 | the four guide-rail strips, the top housing, the side braces, the base footing, the small fittings and the four hot-billet stages |
| `ram_fx_sheet.png` | 1448×1086 | the eight drop-hammer ram phases (travel + impact glow + sparks), the impact-glow discs, the furnace-glow tile, the steam and smoke puffs and the heat wisps |
| `conveyor_sheet.png` | 1448×1086 | twelve conveyor tread segments, the roller frame, an end cap, a support post, a cross brace, a bolt plate, and six dark wall/panel tiles |

## THEY ARE NOT PIXEL ART, AND THE CONVERSION IS NOT AN EXTRACTION

This is the load-bearing fact about this pack and it is measured, not assumed
(the numbers are reproducible with `tools/kit_import.py`'s own predicates):

| | conveyor | ram_fx | frames |
|---|---|---|---|
| unique colours | 109,605 | 159,295 | 144,173 |
| aligned 8×8 blocks fully constant | 0.00% | 0.00% | 0.00% |
| aligned 2×2 blocks fully constant | 8.6% | 8.6% | 6.4% |

...and there is **no integer upscale hiding underneath**: edge energy was
tested against every factor N in 2..12 and sits at chance for all of them, so
there is no smaller grid to recover. These are continuous-tone renders in a
pixel-art *style*. They cannot be sliced on a grid the way `camelot`'s cells
are, and nothing here tries to.

What makes them usable is the **chroma key**: each asset is isolated on
magenta rather than composited into one picture at an unknown scale, so they
can be RESAMPLED to whatever footprint a layer gives them. Automatic
segmentation (row band, then column run with a gap tolerance so a ram's sparks
stay with their ram) finds 51 assets across the three sheets.

The key is **not one colour** — it carries the same grain as the art, so
(248,3,249), (248,4,249) and (248,3,248) are all background. `kit_import.py`
matches it by predicate, converts it to ALPHA *before* any resampling, box
filters premultiplied and thresholds coverage. Resampling first mixes magenta
into every edge pixel and leaves a pink fringe no later quantise removes.

## What the reduction costs, and what it does not

Every pixel is mapped to the nearest entry in the rail's own BG1 ramp set
rather than to a per-asset median cut — nine assets quantised independently
would want 32 colours each against a layer that has 96 for everything. Mapped
into the ramps they use **80 in total**, all inside CGRAM 32..127, so OBJ's
half of CGRAM is untouched.

**The guide-rail strips cannot be used as drawn.** A vertically displaced
column must be identical row to row, and these have caps, feet, bolt courses
and a lighting gradient down their whole length: 38–48 of 52 rows differ from
the modal row even over the middle with the cap and the foot excluded. What
IS taken from them is a **cross-section** — each x is the mean of that column
over the strip's uniform middle, mapped to the palette, then repeated. One row,
invariant by construction, keeping the flute spacing and the metal the art was
drawn with. The art cannot supply the row a displaced column needs; it can
supply the shape.

## Provenance note

Generated art has no upstream licence file to quote and no pack archive to
sha256 against, so the SHA256SUMS here fix *these* files and the paragraph at
the top is the whole chain of custody. `docs/92` records that, and records
that it rests on the owner's statement rather than on a document.
